message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"16","text":"Nevertheless, all of you know that the bishop labors more than all of you, because each of you suffers his own affliction, whereas he suffers both his own and that of each person. Therefore, Clement, take your place at the head as a helper to each person, as far as you are able, burdened with the cares of everyone. Hence I know that, in undertaking to oversee you, I have received a favor, not given one. But take courage and bear it nobly, knowing that when you have reached the harbor of rest, God will repay you with the greatest of good things—an inalienable reward—because you undertook the greater toil for the salvation of all. Thus, if many of the brothers hate you because of righteousness carried to the utmost, their hatred will do you no harm, but the friendship of the righteous God will benefit you greatly. Therefore, strive to shake off praise arising from injustice, but through righteous administration to hunt for the beneficial praise that comes from the Messiah.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"κάμνοντα","chosen":"labors","rationale":"The verb denotes strenuous or wearisome labor."},{"source_quote":"προκαθέσθητι βοηθός","chosen":"take your place at the head as a helper","rationale":"The wording combines a leading or presiding position with service as a helper."},{"source_quote":"τὰς πάντων φορτισθεὶς φροντίδας","chosen":"burdened with the cares of everyone","rationale":"The passive participle depicts Clement as being loaded or burdened with the collective cares."},{"source_quote":"τὸ σὲ οἰκονομεῖν ἀναδέξασθαι","chosen":"in undertaking to oversee you","rationale":"The main rendering provisionally takes Peter as the understood subject of both infinitives and σέ as the object of οἰκονομεῖν; competing analyses remain unresolved."},{"source_quote":"ἀναφαίρετον μισθόν","chosen":"an inalienable reward","rationale":"The adjective describes a reward that cannot be taken away."},{"source_quote":"ἐπ’ ἄκρον δικαιοσύνην","chosen":"righteousness carried to the utmost","rationale":"The expression depicts righteousness extending to its furthest point."},{"source_quote":"ἐκ χριστοῦ","chosen":"from the Messiah","rationale":"Χριστός functions independently as a title here rather than as part of a personal-name construction."},{"source_quote":"θηρεύειν ἔπαινον","chosen":"to hunt for ... praise","rationale":"The rendering preserves the verb’s explicit hunting image and its force of active pursuit."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"τὸ σὲ οἰκονομεῖν ἀναδέξασθαι χάριν οἶδα εἰληφώς, οὐ δεδωκώς","issue":"The assignment of subjects and object remains uncertain. On the analysis selected in the translation, the articular infinitive τὸ σὲ οἰκονομεῖν is the complement of ἀναδέξασθαι, Peter remains the unexpressed subject of both infinitives, and σέ is the direct object of οἰκονομεῖν: Peter undertakes to oversee Clement. This is supported grammatically by the continued first-person perspective and the nominative participles εἰληφώς and δεδωκώς. Alternatively, σέ may be the accusative subject of οἰκονομεῖν, yielding “your administering”; Peter would then undertake the arrangement that Clement administer, an interpretation contextually attractive after Clement’s commission. A further, less explicit analysis makes Clement the subject of ἀναδέξασθαι as well, so that Clement undertakes the administration, but the change of subject is not overtly marked. The image-checked supplied reading does not adjudicate among these analyses and does not itself establish corruption.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":true},{"source_quote":"’σωτηρίας","issue":"The supplied print places a raised apostrophe before σωτηρίας although no elision is apparent. Omitting it would be an orthographic normalization and would not change the translated meaning.","proposed_reading":"σωτηρίας","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"17","text":"After saying these things and more than these, he again looked toward the multitude and said, “And you also, my beloved brothers and fellow servants, yield in every respect to the one presiding over truth, knowing this: whoever grieves this man has not received the Messiah, with whose chair he has been entrusted; and as one who has not received the Messiah, he will be reckoned as having rejected the Father. Therefore, he will be cast out of the good kingdom. For this reason, strive to come to every gathering, so that you may not, as deserters, incur a charge of sin because of the commander’s discouragement. Therefore, above all else, all of you should give thought to his interests, knowing that, because of each of you, the evil one wages war against him alone with greater hostility. So strive to continue in affection toward him and goodwill toward one another, and to obey him, so that he too may be relieved and you may be able to be saved.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"σύνδουλοι","chosen":"fellow servants","rationale":"The term presents the brothers as sharing the status and allegiance of servants."},{"source_quote":"προκαθεζομένῳ ἀληθείας","chosen":"the one presiding over truth","rationale":"The participle denotes occupying the leading seat or presiding position, with truth as its sphere."},{"source_quote":"χριστόν","chosen":"the Messiah","rationale":"The first occurrence functions independently as a title."},{"source_quote":"χριστὸν","chosen":"the Messiah","rationale":"The second occurrence likewise functions independently as a title rather than within a personal name."},{"source_quote":"καθέδραν","chosen":"chair","rationale":"The literal chair represents the entrusted teaching and governing office while preserving the source image."},{"source_quote":"λειποτάκται","chosen":"deserters","rationale":"This is a military term for those who abandon their assigned rank or post."},{"source_quote":"ταξιάρχου","chosen":"commander","rationale":"The military title continues the image introduced by the reference to deserters."},{"source_quote":"ἐπακούειν","chosen":"to obey","rationale":"In this exhortation, the verb conveys heedful compliance rather than merely hearing."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"’ὡς","issue":"The supplied print places a raised apostrophe before ὡς without an evident elision or syntactic function. Omitting it would be an orthographic normalization and would not affect the translation.","proposed_reading":"ὡς","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"18","text":"But you should also understand some things on your own, because he cannot speak openly on account of the plots. For example, if he is hostile to someone, do not wait for him to say, “Do not associate with this person.” Instead, prudently follow his intention, becoming enemies of those to whom he is hostile and not associating with those with whom he does not associate, so that each person, pressing his claim to have everyone as friends, may be saved by reconciling him and heeding his discourse. But if anyone remains a friend to those to whom he is hostile and speaks with those with whom he does not associate, he himself is also one of those who want to destroy the church. For although he is joined with you in body, since he is not with you in purpose, he is against you—far worse than the manifest enemies from outside, scattering those inside under the guise of friendship.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἐν φανερῷ","chosen":"openly","rationale":"The expression contrasts public or unconcealed speech with what must be inferred because of plots."},{"source_quote":"προσαμιλλᾶσθαι","chosen":"associate with","rationale":"The verb can denote engaging or contending with someone, but the surrounding references to friendship and conversation support a relational sense."},{"source_quote":"βουλήματι","chosen":"intention","rationale":"The noun denotes the leader’s purpose or will, which the audience is expected to discern."},{"source_quote":"ἐπιδικαζόμενος τοῦ πάντας φίλους ἔχειν","chosen":"pressing his claim to have everyone as friends","rationale":"The middle participle conveys asserting or pressing a claim, not merely seeking an outcome."},{"source_quote":"αὐτὸν διαλλάττων","chosen":"reconciling him","rationale":"The rendering preserves αὐτόν as the direct object of the active participle without supplying an unexpressed second party or replacing the unresolved pronoun with a named referent."},{"source_quote":"ὁμιλίας","chosen":"discourse","rationale":"The noun here refers to speech, conversation, or instruction that is to be heeded."},{"source_quote":"γνώμῃ","chosen":"purpose","rationale":"The term denotes inward judgment or intention, contrasted with bodily presence."},{"source_quote":"τῶν ἔξωθεν φαινομένων ἐχθρῶν","chosen":"the manifest enemies from outside","rationale":"The rendering preserves both their evident enmity and their position outside, in contrast with those inside."},{"source_quote":"μετὰ δοκούσης φιλίας","chosen":"under the guise of friendship","rationale":"The participle marks the friendship as seeming or apparent rather than genuine."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἵνα ἕκαστος, ἐπιδικαζόμενος τοῦ πάντας φίλους ἔχειν, αὐτὸν διαλλάττων σώζηται","issue":"The referent of αὐτόν and the relationship expressed by διαλλάττων remain unresolved. The presiding leader is the most continuously salient singular masculine referent: the preceding clauses repeatedly use αὐτός and αὐτοῦ for him, whereas the intervening οἷς is plural and denotes those to whom he is hostile. Contextually, communal withdrawal could compel an alienated person who wants everyone as friends to reconcile the leader or win him over. Grammatically, however, αὐτόν is the direct object of active διαλλάττων; the construction explicitly presents him as the affected person but does not state the other party to the reconciliation. It can therefore be understood as reconciling the leader, winning him over, or elliptically effecting reconciliation with him. A less likely but possible interpretation takes αὐτόν as another alienated person. The translation retains the pronoun and direct-object construction because the supplied wording does not settle these materially different relationships.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":true},{"source_quote":"τῆς αὐτοῦ ἐπακούων ὁμιλίας","issue":"The possessive αὐτοῦ most naturally continues the paragraph’s recurring reference to the presiding leader, particularly the earlier αὐτοῦ τῷ βουλήματι, and this reading makes obedience to his discourse the culmination of following his intention. Nevertheless, the immediately preceding αὐτὸν διαλλάττων introduces an unresolved personal referent, and αὐτοῦ can grammatically refer to that same person. If αὐτόν denotes an alienated person rather than the leader, whose discourse is heeded changes accordingly. The main text therefore preserves the neutral pronoun while the antecedent remains unresolved.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":true}]},{"reference":"19","text":"After saying these things, there in the midst before everyone, he laid his hands on me and urged me to sit in his own chair. When I had sat down, he immediately said this to me: “Before all my brothers who are present with me, I ask you that, whenever I depart from this life here—as is owed to me—you not hesitate to send James, the Lord’s brother, a concise written account extending even to your thoughts from childhood and telling how, from the beginning until now, you have traveled with me, listening to the words and deeds proclaimed by me from city to city, and then, toward the end, also to make known the cause of my death, as I said beforehand. For this will not grieve him greatly, since he knows that I have piously paid what I was inevitably bound to suffer. Rather, he will obtain the greatest consolation when he learns that after me it was not to an unlearned man—one ignorant of life-giving words and not knowing the church’s rule—that the teacher’s chair was entrusted. For misleading discourse destroys the souls of the crowds who hear it.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἐδυσώπησεν","chosen":"urged","rationale":"The verb means to prevail upon or strongly entreat someone."},{"source_quote":"Ἀξιῶ σε","chosen":"I ask you","rationale":"The verb introduces Peter’s formal request before the witnesses who are present."},{"source_quote":"σὲ Ἰακώβῳ τῷ ἀδελφῷ τοῦ κυρίου διαπέμψαι ἐν ἐπιτομῇ ἀναγραψάμενον","chosen":"you not hesitate to send James, the Lord’s brother, a concise written account","rationale":"The translation provisionally treats the second σέ as a resumed accusative subject of διαπέμψαι and ἀναγραψάμενον, with the written account understood from the act of recording in epitome; the extended syntax remains unresolved."},{"source_quote":"λογισμῶν","chosen":"thoughts","rationale":"The noun denotes thoughts, considerations, or reasonings extending back to Clement’s childhood."},{"source_quote":"κηρυχθέντων","chosen":"proclaimed","rationale":"The participle grammatically applies to both the words and the deeds, an unusual coordination retained in English."},{"source_quote":"πρόφασιν","chosen":"cause","rationale":"The noun can mean cause, occasion, or pretext; the requested account of Peter’s death supports “cause.”"},{"source_quote":"ὡς προεῖπον","chosen":"as I said beforehand","rationale":"This preserves the temporal force of προ- without requiring the more specific claim that the prior statement was a prophecy."},{"source_quote":"πάντως ἔδει με παθεῖν","chosen":"I was inevitably bound to suffer","rationale":"Πάντως reinforces the certainty or inevitability of the necessary suffering."},{"source_quote":"ἀπεδόμην","chosen":"I have ... paid","rationale":"The aorist middle presents the necessary suffering as an obligation rendered or discharged."},{"source_quote":"κανόνα","chosen":"rule","rationale":"The noun denotes an authoritative norm or standard and need not refer to a later fixed collection of writings."},{"source_quote":"πλάνος","chosen":"misleading","rationale":"The adjective characterizes the discourse as leading its hearers astray."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"καθεσθῆναί με. ἐδυσώπησεν","issue":"The printed period separates the infinitive from the finite verb that most naturally governs it. The translation construes the words together while preserving the period as an editorial feature of the supplied edition; this punctuation does not by itself demonstrate textual corruption.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"Ἀξιῶ σε ἐπὶ πάντων μου τῶν συνπαρόντων ἀδελφῶν, ὅπως ὁπόταν τοῦ ἐνταῦθα (ὡς ἐμοὶ ὀφείλεται) ἀπαλλάξω βίου, σὲ Ἰακώβῳ τῷ ἀδελφῷ τοῦ κυρίου διαπέμψαι ἐν ἐπιτομῇ ἀναγραψάμενον μέχρι καὶ τῶν ἐκ παίδων σου λογισμῶν καὶ ὡς ἀπ᾽ ἀρχῆς μέχρι τοῦ νῦν συνώδευσάς μοι, ἐπακούων τῶν κατὰ πόλιν ὑπ᾽ ἐμοῦ κηρυχθέντων λόγων τε καὶ πράξεων, ἔπειτα πρὸς τῷ τέλει καὶ τὴν τοῦ θανάτου μου πρόφασιν ὡς προεῖπον δηλῶσαι μὴ ὀκνήσῃς","issue":"The relationships among Ἀξιῶ σε, ὅπως, the resumed σέ, the infinitives διαπέμψαι and δηλῶσαι, and the final μὴ ὀκνήσῃς remain syntactically unsettled. The main translation takes Ἀξιῶ σε with the ὅπως request, treats μὴ ὀκνήσῃς as the finite conclusion governing both infinitival instructions, and understands the sense as “I ask you … not to hesitate to send … and then, toward the end, also to make known …”. The final position of μὴ ὀκνήσῃς and the coordination of the two requested acts support that scope. The second σέ is then read as a resumptive accusative subject after the intervening temporal clause, with ἀναγραψάμενον agreeing with it, although a complementary infinitive with the same subject as ὀκνήσῃς would ordinarily omit that subject. Alternatively, σέ may be the object of διαπέμψαι, “send yourself to James,” though a reflexive form would be more expected; or μὴ ὀκνήσῃς may attach explicitly only to δηλῶσαι, leaving διαπέμψαι more directly dependent on the earlier request. The supplied wording and image-checked punctuation do not settle these alternatives or independently establish corruption.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":true},{"source_quote":"οὐκ ἀμαθὴς ἀνὴρ καὶ ζωοποιοὺς λόγους ἀγνοῶν καὶ ἐκκλησίας κανόνα. οὐκ εἰδὼς τὴν τοῦ διδάσκοντος ἐπιστεύθη καθέδραν","issue":"The scope of the first οὐκ remains uncertain. The main translation takes οὐκ as excluding the whole described recipient from the entrusting: it was not to an unlearned man—one ignorant of life-giving words and explicitly described by οὐκ εἰδώς as not knowing the church’s rule—that the chair was entrusted. This reading fits the delayed verb ἐπιστεύθη and the stated consolation obtained from learning who succeeded Peter. Formally, however, οὐκ stands immediately before ἀμαθής and can locally produce “a not-unlearned man,” after which the positive participle ἀγνοῶν and the explicitly negated οὐκ εἰδώς create a difficult coordination. The conjunctions καί do not independently establish that the first negation distributes across all the descriptions. Both negations are preserved in the translation, but the syntax does not securely determine whether the first negates only ἀμαθής or the larger proposition concerning the recipient of the chair.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":true},{"source_quote":"κανόνα. οὐκ εἰδὼς","issue":"The printed period interrupts the description before οὐκ εἰδώς. The translation treats the participle as continuing the description while retaining the period as an editorial feature of the supplied edition; the punctuation alone is not evidence of textual corruption or a resolution of the negation’s scope.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"20","text":"Therefore I, my lord James, after he had said these things and I had made my promise, did not hesitate, as I had been commanded, to present in outline the greater part of the discourses from city to city, which had already been written to you beforehand and sent by him in books, as a kind of reminder, and in this form to send them to you, giving the work the title “Clement’s Epitome of Peter’s Sojourn-Preachings.” But I will begin to set it out as I was commanded.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ὑποσχόμενος","chosen":"I had made my promise","rationale":"The participle records Clement’s promise before describing his prompt fulfillment of it."},{"source_quote":"τὸ πολὺ","chosen":"the greater part","rationale":"The expression denotes the bulk or most of the material rather than necessarily all of it."},{"source_quote":"ἐπὶ κεφαλαίων ποιῆσαι","chosen":"to present in outline","rationale":"The phrase concerns reducing or presenting the material by principal points, not merely placing otherwise unabridged material beneath headings."},{"source_quote":"σημείου χάριν","chosen":"as a kind of reminder","rationale":"Literally involving a sign or marker, the phrase describes the summary as an aid to recognition or recollection."},{"source_quote":"ἐπιδημίων κηρυγμάτων","chosen":"Sojourn-Preachings","rationale":"The source-qualified compound preserves the adjective as a direct modifier of “preachings” without converting it into an explicit temporal clause such as “during his sojourns”; the adjective’s precise contextual force remains unresolved."},{"source_quote":"ἐκτιθέναι","chosen":"set it out","rationale":"The verb marks the transition from the prefatory letter to presenting the promised material."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἐπιγράψαντα","issue":"The accusative participle is syntactically marked with the first-person subject of οὐκ ὤκνησα. It may agree with an understood accusative subject of the dependent infinitives. The nominative ἐπιγράψας would be a conjectural normalization, not an established correction to the supplied reading.","proposed_reading":"ἐπιγράψας","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"Κλήμεντος τῶν Πέτρου ἐπιδημίων κηρυγμάτων ἐπιτομή","issue":"The adjective ἐπιδημίων directly and attributively qualifies κηρυγμάτων; it is not an explicit temporal phrase modifying an act of preaching. Its lexical association with presence in a place, sojourning, or visiting supports understanding the preachings as characterized by Peter’s sojourns or visits, and the preceding description of discourses κατὰ πόλιν gives contextual support to a visit-associated sense. Nevertheless, the adjective can also bear a local or public sense connected with being in a place or among its people, and the title does not specify whether the relationship is temporal, circumstantial, or classificatory. “Sojourn-Preachings” is therefore a deliberately source-qualified provisional rendering, while alternatives such as “preachings during Peter’s sojourns,” “visit-preachings,” or “local/public preachings” remain unresolved. No change to the supplied Greek is proposed.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":true}]}]}
